content: A brave warrior does not run from the storm; he runs directly into it, knowing that the fastest way through is head-on.
author: Native American Proverbs
sourceWork: Bison Folklore of the Great Plains
explanation: When a blizzard sweeps across the prairie, cattle instinctively turn their backs and try to outrun the gale, keeping them trapped in the freezing storm for days until they collapse. The American bison does the opposite: it turns its massive head directly into the freezing wind and charges through, minimizing the time spent in the storm. Face your trials head-on.
practicalInsight: Stop procrastinating on that dreaded task or difficult conversation. Charge directly into it today and get to the other side.
reflectionPrompt: What difficult challenge are you trying to run away from that you need to face head-on like the bison?
